issue_context.title: Expose cppgc::CppHeap::CollectStatistics() in v8 module
issue_context.body:
### What is the problem this feature will solve?

Since we've been migrating things to use `CppHeap`, we have a bunch of extra GC-managed memory which has become a bit less mysterious to V8. This means we can take better advantage of V8 interfaces to get observability into this memory.

### What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?

It would likely be an easy win to expose `CppHeap` data via [`cppgc::CppHeap::CollectStatistics()`](https://v8docs.nodesource.com/node-22.4/d9/dc4/classv8_1_1_cpp_heap.html#a3a5d09567758e608fffde50eeabc2feb) in the `v8` module.

cc @nodejs/diagnostics 

### What alternatives have you considered?

_No response_
comments: Given the support for this, I'd like to start working on it!

review_comments: The string argument would lead to repeated V8 string -> C++ string conversion costs (and in our current `Utf8Value` implementation, repeated latin-1 -> UTF8 transcoding on the constants every time it's invoked). I think the boolean could make the API difficult to extend if V8 adds another detail level in the future.
Yes but this is quite unlikely to be a hot path so I'm not too concerned about performance and would rather simplify the js side of the code a bit more.

If it's a string to the C++ land, then the C++ land needs to do the string to enum mapping instead of just static_cast, leaving the complexity to C++ instead (unless we want to clamp a V8 enum into a boolean, which could make future extensions difficult once it has more than 2 values..).

> Yes but this is quite unlikely to be a hot path so I'm not too concerned about performance

If this is used by performance tracing then the overhead likely matters (or from https://github.com/nodejs/node/pull/4463, why v8.getHeapStatistics() is optimized to be the way it is, and my impression is that APIs used for tracing statistics generally have this tendency of prioritizing overhead reduction over simplicity). It seems better to be consistent.
